title: Correlative Light- and Electron Microscopy Using Quantum Dot Nanoparticles
protocol: Dissect tissue pieces from a surgically resected tumor specimen or tissue biopsy.
Prepare a stock buffer solution by adding 21.4 g of sodium cacodylate and 3.0 ml of 1% calcium chloride solution to 90 ml of distilled water, then topping up the solution to a final volume of 100 ml.
Stir the stock buffer solution and leave it to stand overnight to dissolve crystalline reagent completely.
Prepare a buffer working solution by adding 20 ml of stock solution to 170 ml of water.
Check the pH of the buffer working solution with indicator strips.
Adjust the pH to 7.4 by adding 3 - 4 drops of 3% HCl if necessary.
Top up the final buffer working solution volume to 200 ml with a final molarity of 0.1 M.
Add one 10 ml ampoule of 50% glutaraldehyde solution to 20 ml of sodium cacodylate stock solution (1 M).
Top up the fixative mixture with distilled water to 190 ml.
Check the pH of the fixative and adjust to 7.4 by adding 1 - 4 drops of 3% hydrochloric acid if necessary.
Top up the final fixative volume to 200 ml.
Immerse the tissue in fixative containing 2.5% glutaraldehyde in 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer pH 7.4 for 24 hours at 4°C.
Discard unused fixative after one week.
Wash the tissue with 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer for 20 minutes.
Repeat washing the tissue with 0.1 M sodium cacodylate buffer for another 20 minutes.

Prepare a 2% aqueous osmium tetroxide working solution by mixing 8.0 ml of a 5% OsO4 stock solution, 2.0 ml of sodium cacodylate buffer (1 M), and 10.0 ml of distilled water to make a final volume of 20.0 ml.
Immerse the tissue in 2% osmium tetroxide at pH 7.4 for 4 hours at room temperature.
Remove the OsO4 solution from the tissue after incubation.
Wash the tissue with 2% sodium acetate for 10 minutes.
Immerse the tissue in 2% uranyl acetate for 1 hour at room temperature.

Dehydrate the tissue through graded alcohols: use 50% ethanol for 10 minutes, 70% ethanol for 10 minutes, 95% ethanol for 10 minutes, and two changes of 100% ethanol for 20 minutes each at room temperature.
Perform two changes of 100% acetone for 30 minutes each.
Mix low-viscosity epoxy resin in a disposable polyethylene cup.
Add 10.0 g of vinyl cyclohexene dioxide (ERL 4221) epoxy monomer, 6 g of diglycidyl ether of polypropylene glycol (DER 732), and 26.0 g of nonenyl succinic anhydride (NSA).
Stir thoroughly by hand using wooden sticks for 2 min.
Add fifteen drops of 2-dimethylaminoethanol (DMAE) epoxy accelerator and stir again for 2 min.
Start resin impregnation of the tissue by replacing 100% acetone with a 1:1 mixture of resin to acetone for 1 hour.
Replace with a 6:1 mixture of resin to acetone for 3 hours.
Finally, replace with 100% resin overnight.
Transfer the tissue into fresh resin in 8 mm micromoulds.
Cure at 70°C overnight.
Place a semithin diamond knife in the ultramicrotome and cut sections from the tissue at a thickness of 500 nm.
Float sections onto the water bath behind the knife edge.
Pick up the sections on a glass slide.
Dry the sections down for 10 to 20 seconds using a hotplate at approximately 110°C.
Etch the sections with sodium ethoxide solution for 20 seconds.
Wash off with 100% ethanol.
Rinse with distilled water.
Stain with 2% methylene blue in 1% borax for 20 seconds on the hotplate.
Rinse with running tap water for 5 seconds.
Dry on the hotplate for 5 seconds.
Stain with 1.5% basic fuchsin on the hotplate for 5 seconds.
Dry on the hotplate for 20 seconds.
Examine by bright-field light microscopy to confirm tumor cells and ROI presence in the section.
Change the semithin diamond knife to an ultrathin diamond knife.
Set the correct knife angle and cutting speed as recommended by the knife manufacturer.
Cut ultrathin sections at 90 nm thickness.
Observe gold coloration of the sections when floating on the water bath.
Stretch and flatten the sections using chloroform vapor from a filter paper within a few millimeters of the sections.
Lift up the ultrathin sections from the water surface using a 300-mesh thin-bar nickel TEM grid dipped in section adhesive solution.
Locate the sections on the dull side of the grid.
Place 20 cm of clear adhesive tape in a 5 ml vial with 2.0 ml of acetone.
Cap and shake the vial.
Let stand for 10 min then remove the tape leaving the adhesive solution.
Prepare 1 ml of fresh saturated sodium metaperiodate etching solution in distilled water.
Use the etching solution immediately.
Place droplets of the etching solution on a clean labfilm surface.
Place completely dry grids with sections down on droplets of sodium metaperiodate solution at room temperature for 30 min.
Transfer the grids to distilled water droplets for 60 sec of washing.
Place the grid on a droplet of 0.05 M glycine in PBS for 10 min to block residual aldehyde in the section.
Remove the aldehyde block by briefly blotting the edge of the grid.
Place the grid on a droplet of 1% normal goat serum (NGS) and 1% BSAc (10%) in PBS for 10 min.
Prepare the blocking solution by adding 10 μl of NGS and 100 μl of BSAc to 890 μl of PBS to give a final volume of 1,000 μl.
Condition the sections by placing on a droplet of antibody diluent for 10 min.
Perform the immunolabeling incubation using anti-somatostatin polyclonal antibody diluted 1:10 with antibody diluent giving a concentration of 3.47 g/L.
Note: Antibody incubation is done by placing grids on droplets for 1 hr at room temperature in a moist chamber.
Remove antibody reagent by blotting the edge of the grid.
Wash sections on diluent for 2 x 5 min.
Incubate in secondary antibody (biotinylated goat anti-rabbit polyclonal) diluted 1:10 for 1 hr at room temperature.
Remove the secondary antibody solution.
Wash in diluent for 2 x 5 min.
Incubate in streptavidin conjugated QDs (585 nm) diluted 1:10 for 1 hr at room temperature.
Cover with aluminum foil to reduce light exposure during the incubation.
Wash grids in fresh distilled water for 2 min.
Blot the edges of the grid dry.
Use 365 nm light emitting diode (LED) illumination for wide-field fluorescence light microscopy.
Insert a filter cube with Ex G 365 nm, BS FT 395, and EM LP 420 nm characteristics.
Place the immunostained grid section down on a glass slide in a droplet of water.
Cover the immunostained grid section with a glass cover slip (thickness number 1.5).
Use light microscopy to evaluate the labeling pattern.
Establish that negative controls are clear of labeling.
Identify ROI in relation to grid bars.
Acquire images of positive labeling on the section using a full color digital camera with settings at "FL auto colour" and "White Balance" set at 3,200K.
Use the camera in "Automatic exposure" mode with a "Gamma" setting between 0.45 and 1.00 to optimize image appearance and "Analog Gain" set at 1x.
Click the camera icon in the Zen 2 Lite software graphical interface to "Live".
Focus the image then click "Snap" to capture the image to the framestore.
Save images as .tif files to avoid compression and pixelation.
Prepare a print showing the position of the ROI in relation to grid bars or other significant tissue landmarks.
Remove the grid from the slide.
Wash the slide in distilled water.
Gently blot the edges dry.
Transfer the grid to the TEM for examination using an accelerating voltage of 100 kV.
Navigate around the grid and find regions of interest (ROIs) that correlate with light microscopy views using low magnification of approximately 1,400X.
View clusters of QDs at magnifications around 50,000X.
Observe individual QDs at 70,000X magnification or above.
Acquire images by clicking the "Camera" icon to "On" in the microscope graphical interface and then to "Off" to store the image in the framestore.
Save images as .tif files.
Locate corresponding ROIs by TEM using a print from the light microscopy image.
Use tissue architectural features such as blood vessels and luminal structures for navigation.
Capture an image of the ROI by TEM.
Ensure the TEM image is correctly orientated with the light microscopy image.
Correct the enlargement of both images so that the same structure appears the same size in each modality.
Orientate the light microscopy and TEM images to display them side-by-side or as overlays.
Enlarge the fluorescence image to match the magnification of a low power TEM image.
Select the fluorescence image using the "Rectangular Marquee Tool".
Create a duplicate layer from the selected fluorescence image.
Adjust the "Layer Style/Blending options" to 30 - 40% transparency.
Drag the fluorescence overlay layer over the corresponding TEM image using the "Move Tool".
Align both images carefully.
Flatten the layers after alignment to produce the final overlay image.
Select the new overlay image using the "Rectangular Marquee Tool".
Copy the selected overlay image to a new canvas.
Save the final overlay image as a .tiff file.
